Indian tribes operating Head Start programs may establish their own selection criteria to prioritize children in families with a tribal member, effective this fiscal year and annually thereafter.

**Working Notes — Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2024 (Part 10/11)**

**Sec. 7034 (cont.) — General Provisions**

- **(e) Partner Vetting:** Secretary of State and USAID Administrator must consult Appropriations Committees before initiating/modifying partner vetting programs. Must provide direct vetting option for prime awardees unless case-by-case infeasibility determination. May restrict/terminate awards based on vetting info.
- **(f) Contingencies:** President may use up to $125,000,000 under FAA §451 during FY2024, notwithstanding other law.
- **(g) International Child Abductions:** Secretary should withhold title III funds from central governments of countries not complying with the Hague Convention on Civil Aspects of International Child Abductions. Report to Appropriations within 15 days of withholding.
- **(h) Transfer for Extraordinary Protection:** Secretary may transfer up to $50,000,000 of expired unobligated "Diplomatic Programs" balances to "Protection of Foreign Missions and Officials," no later than end of 5th fiscal year after last availability.
- **(i) Protections for Employees of Diplomatic Missions/International Organizations:** Extends §7034(k) of FY2020 appropriations (P.L. 116-94) through FY2024.
- **(j) Impact on Jobs:** Extends §7056 of FY2021 appropriations (P.L. 116-260) through FY2024.
- **(k) Extension of Authorities:**
  - (1) Critical posts incentives (§1115(d), P.L. 111-32) extended through Sept. 30, 2024.
  - (2) Categorical eligibility: Amends §599D and §599E of P.L. 101-167, replacing "2023" with "2024."
  - (3) SIGAR competitive status: Employees with 12+ months continuous service or employed at SIGAR termination acquire competitive service status.
  - (4) Transfer of balances: §7081(h) of FY2017 appropriations (P.L. 115-31) extended through FY2024.
  - (5) Protective services: §7071 of FY2022 appropriations (P.L. 117-103) extended through FY2024; cap raised from $30M to $40M.
  - (6) Israel loan guarantees: Amends P.L. 108-11, extending deadline from Sept. 30, 2028 to Sept. 30, 2029.
  - (7) Personal services contract authority (§2401, P.L. 117-43) extended through Sept. 30, 2024.
- **(l) Monitoring and Evaluation:**
  - (1) Beneficiary feedback: Funds for M&E under Development Assistance, International Disaster Assistance, Migration and Refugee Assistance must support systematic beneficiary feedback collection. Within 90 days, Secretary and USAID Administrator must submit and post updated procedures.
  - (2) Evaluations: Not less than $15,000,000 from titles III and IV for impact evaluations (remain available until expended); $10,000,000 coordinated with USAID Office of Chief Economist. In addition to other funds.
- **(m) HIV/AIDS Working Capital Fund:** May be used for child survival, malaria, TB, emerging infectious disease pharmaceuticals to same extent as HIV/AIDS, subject to §525(b) terms. Authority exercised by USAID Assistant Administrator for Global Health, subject to regular notification. Secretary must include accounting in budget justification.
- **(n) Local Works:**
  - (1) Not less than $100,000,000 from Development Assistance and ESF for Local Works (§7080, P.L. 113-235), available until Sept. 30, 2028.
  - (2) "Eligible entities" = small NGOs, educational institutions, other small entities receiving less than $5,000,000 from USAID over prior 5 fiscal years. Departments/centers of educational institutions considered individually.
- **(o) Procurement Authority:** §7077 of FY2012 appropriations (P.L. 112-74) extended through FY2024.
- **(p) Extension:** §7034(r) of FY2022 appropriations (P.L. 117-103) applies during FY2024.
- **(q) Staff Care for Afghan Nationals:** Up to $50,000 may be used by USAID for services to former locally employed staff of USAID Afghanistan mission.
- **(r) War Crimes Accountability:** Not less than $5,000,000 from ESF for purposes authorized by §2015 of P.L. 107-206 (as amended), including not less than $2,500,000 for Trust Fund for Victims.
- **(s) Definitions:** Defines "appropriate congressional committees," "funds appropriated by this Act and prior Acts," "international financial institutions" (lists 13 institutions), "Pacific Islands countries" (lists 14 countries), "spend plan," "successor operating unit," and "USAID."

**Sec. 7035 — Law Enforcement and Security**

- **(a)(1) Community-based police assistance:** Funds under titles III and IV may be used notwithstanding FAA §660 for civilian police training in human rights, rule of law, anti-corruption, etc.
- **(a)(2) Combat casualty care:** Peacekeeping Operations and FMF funds must be available for combat casualty training/equipment above prior year level. Secretary must offer such training/equipment with lethal assistance
